title: The Northern Circuit of Tanzania Explained
excerpt: The northern circuit is Tanzania's classic safari route: Tarangire, Manyara, Ngorongoro and the Serengeti, starting from Arusha.
body:
When people talk about a safari in Tanzania, they usually mean the northern circuit. It is a loop of famous parks starting and ending in Arusha.

## The parks

- **[Tarangire](/blog/tarangire-national-park-guide/):** elephants and baobabs.
- **[Lake Manyara](/blog/lake-manyara-guide/):** forest, lake and birds.
- **[Ngorongoro Crater](/blog/ngorongoro-crater-guide/):** wildlife in a caldera.
- **[Serengeti](/blog/serengeti-national-park-guide/):** endless plains and the migration.
- Extras: [Arusha National Park](/blog/arusha-national-park-guide/), [Lake Natron](/blog/lake-natron-guide/), [Lake Eyasi](/blog/lake-eyasi-guide/).

## A typical route

Arusha → Tarangire → Manyara or Karatu → Serengeti (two or three nights) → Ngorongoro → Arusha. Five to eight days.

## Why it is popular

Excellent wildlife all year, good roads and lodges, and easy combinations with Kilimanjaro and Zanzibar.

## Downside

In high season, popular areas can get busy. Choosing the right regions in the Serengeti and good timing helps.

## Alternatives

For quiet and wild, consider the [southern circuit](/blog/southern-circuit-tanzania/).
